I do not see an insight inquiry but given the amount of questions via teams I will answer a few.

I reviewed the campaign and can confirm that the budget allocation is and has been set up correctly since launch, with 80% dedicated to lighting and 20% dedicated to landscaping. As discussed, this is split 40%/40% for lighting and 10%/10% for landscaping across each location.


While landscaping may currently show more impressions based on the screenshots you provided via Teams, those screenshots do not reflect budget allocation, and impressions do not indicate that a campaign is receiving more budget. The budgets are set and allocated accordingly, and landscaping cannot spend more than the budget assigned to it. Impressions simply reflect how often users are searching for and triggering ads related to that service.


At this time, the data suggests that landscaping-related searches are generating more opportunities to serve ads, while lighting-related searches are occurring less frequently. As a result, landscaping may accumulate more impressions even while operating under a significantly smaller budget allocation than lighting.

In short, the impression volume is being driven by user search behavior, not by a shift in budget away from lighting. The budget distribution remains aligned with the intended 80/20 split.

It's also important to note that a client searching for their own ads or service is not a reliable way to evaluate campaign performance. Google does not show ads on every search and uses factors such as location, search history, device, timing, and auction competition to determine when an ad appears. Repeatedly searching for your own ads can also influence what you see over time and may create a misleading impression of campaign visibility. For this reason, we rely on the actual campaign data, impressions, clicks, and conversions within Google Ads rather than manual searches to evaluate performance.

Please also keep in mind that the campaign has only been live for approximately 14 days and we have already 18 conversions which is great. We typically recommend allowing 30–60 days to gather sufficient data and give Google's system time to optimize before drawing conclusions from early performance trends. Despite being live for a relatively short period, the campaign has already generated conversions, which indicates that the ads are serving and reaching potential customers.

I will continue monitoring performance and search demand across both services in my monthly opts and make recommendations if adjustments become necessary.

-we're not using any content suitability restrictions right now - so can't open up volume that way

-replacing search with a demand gen campaign is another strategy - demand gen campaigns are specifically designed for awareness objectives
-we're already using the least restrictive bid strategy for pmax with max conversions - we are not using any bid limits such as a troas or tCPA
-I expanded the audience signals by added first party data
-Another idea we could try, set your LPV goals up as a primary conversion to optimize towards (ex career and get started page views).  This would then change the algorithm and tell Google to optimize towards those most likely to click and land on a page vs actually making contact. This tactic would most likely allow us to enter into more auctions and increase imps. But, keep in mind its a strategic tradeoff of actually getting a true lead via call.
-Did we ever hear back from the DCM on why we are not tracking actual website calls? That would be another suggestion to keep providing Google with strong data signals on who to keep showing the ads to
-Ultimately, if we want to increase impressions, our biggest impact would be increasing budget since we are limited by budget right now. I've never heard of us guaranteeing a certain number of impressions, as pmax is meant to be a conversion based tactic. Our current campaign settings aren't too restrictive, but still strategically targeted to the relevant audience. Consider either putting pmax and search on a fluid budget, and moving more budget into pmax. If our goal is 100% awareness, we could also run a fluid budget with pmax and demand gen, putting majority of our budget into pmax since that still contains search and captures high intent. Then allocate a small portion, say 20% to demand gen to boost top of funnel impressions cheaply.

subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

antonios notes
Big Sky Outdoor Space Notes:
-In some accounts, I’ve seen improved performance when enabling the auto-apply settings “Use optimized ad rotation” and “Use optimized targeting.” These can be found under Recommendations → Auto-apply settings, and may help with overall optimization.
 
-Since the account has a large number of product images, we may want to test enabling Dynamic Images under Account-Level Automated Assets to potentially improve ad engagement.
 
-I noticed a Location Extension is already set up. Would it make sense to also enable “Add store visits as an account default goal” within the auto-apply settings? This could help encourage more local showroom traffic.
 
-Given the large number of gallery images (BBQs, hot tubs, pools, etc.), this account could potentially benefit from testing a Performance Max campaign, as these products are very visual. Budget may be a limiting factor, but we could consider testing a 50/50 split between Search and PMax to see if visual placements drive incremental performance.
 
-For the Hot Tub ad group, we may want to test ad copy tailored to the local climate, such as “Built for Montana Winters” or “Relax Even When Temperatures Drop Below Zero.”
 
-We should also lean further into tap-to-call CTAs and location-based headlines such as “Visit Our Missoula Showroom”, particularly for mobile users. Over the last 30 days, most traffic and spend has come from mobile, and 4 conversions were driven by mobile, indicating strong local, high-intent behavior.
 
-Over the last 30 days, Hot Tub ad group spend increased from $71 to $365, surpassing the Custom BBQ ad group in spend, but without generating conversions. It may be worth investigating why this increase in traffic hasn’t translated into conversions, whether due to search intent, landing page alignment, or query quality.
 
- Maybe also consider adding values to your conversion actions to push google to prioritize calls for example over the local action conversions that we have for website visits and "other engagements".

Hello, The campaign is pretty much totally QA'd aside for the keywords. I see the doc you uploaded labeled "keywords from website" has almost 2k keywords on it that is way too many. If you try to run 2,000 keywords on a $1,500 budget, the spend gets spread too thin and hurts performance. Most keywords won’t get enough clicks or data for Google to optimize, which slows learning and wastes money on low-quality terms. It also lowers impression share on your best keywords, makes the account harder to manage, and increases the risk of irrelevant clicks. A better approach is to focus budget on a smaller set of high-intent keywords, then expand once you have enough data to see what works. We have 4 ad groups, I think 20 in each ad group is more than enough. Would the client like to pick the top 80 keywords or would you like to leave that to my discretion? subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

One of the biggest contributors was the Stewart Tennis Courts & Fencing, Inc. Courts/Georgia #2 campaign, which increased from 1 click to 20 clicks, resulting in a +1900% increase. Another key factor was campaign eligibility. The Georgia #2 campaigns were previously eligible only about 37% of the time, but during the most recent period they were eligible 100% of the time. This means the ads were active and able to serve for a longer duration, which naturally increased the opportunity to generate clicks. There were also targeting updates and keyword additions. A branded keyword — “stewart tennis courts & fencing inc” — was added to the Brand ad group. This likely helped capture more high-intent searches from users specifically looking for the company, which contributed to the overall click growth. subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Opts 9.13
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
KPI is traffic/page views. Performing well, but since the July our CPC has been steadily increasing. It's fairly common for physical therapy and a lot of similar medical industries involving movement to see decreased performance towards the end of summer, but we will be monitoring it closely to make sure it's seasonality and not something else.
    We're still seeing huge impression volume (over 400,000 in August) which is driving down our CTR. We've added exclusions each round of opts, but the campaign is still likely seeing too many placements and is still struggling to identify the most valuable audiences. 
    Normally after this many months the impression share is much lower and the campaign functions similarly to a search campaign in that it becomes more focused, but this one is still spread out really far. 
    It's performing well for the budget, and our conversion rate is still over 11%, but it could probably be higher if we could get it a bit more focused. We've added some more search themes and exclusions so hopefully we start moving in that direction.

subtasks.title: 11/20/23 Opts
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: 15 Day Opts
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

Notes to Tan-I completed the 15 day opt on all 3 campaigns. Here are the main points, but let's schedule a call this week so we can discuss in more detail.
-This is an awareness campaign, but we aren't generating many clicks. Only 79 clicks total between all 3 campaigns
-One observation, our CPC is higher than expected, and I think we can fix this with better ad copy and/or a landing page and really tighten up which keywords we want to target
-This campaign is unusual to me, and I need a better understanding of why we are using the keywords requested to be directed to the Together We're More Site. For example, on the OKC and ADA campaigns, majority of our budget is going through our Choctaw ad group, primary keyword "Choctaw Nation". The searches I am seeing are "Choctaw People", "Choctaw resort" "conctaw concerts", "Choctaw Cultural Center", I also a lot of searches for "dawes rolls" under the Tusla campaign - I had to look this up, is a way to trace your ancestry. Are these the types of searches they want directed to this site?   
-Overall, I'm finding it hard to optimize this campaign because I don't really understand why we are sending some of this traffic to our website. For example, why are bidding on the Cultural Center or the Choctaw Casino but then our ads or website mention nothing about this? I think that is part of the reason why we are seeing higher CPC's.
-This month we're supposed to be promoting Charles Shadle, majority of our keywords are not serving because of low search volume. I'm using broad keyword match and its still shows low volume. We're also using a lot of keywords, so the budget will spend where it sees the most traffic.
-There is also little traffic to the "Together We're More" and very little imps on the other artists too, even using broad match types

I think we need to really focus on what traffic they want directed to the site, and does our website content match what those searches are looking for. I can then change the ad copy too, majority of the ad copy was used from what was on the site, but that's not matching up directly with our kw's. Ultimatley, we need to look at our kw's list and ask ourselves, does this make sense? Many of the keywords or themes, are already being used on the Choctaw Cultural Center's campaign. This campaign could be more focused on the "Together We're More" or artists spotlight, and maybe we can cut back on a lot of the more generic kw's.

It could be too early, but I also think this would be better if we could add a demand gen campaign if awareness if the objective.  I know we are dealing with a budget constraint, maybe we can take the budget from one of the smaller populations like Ada, and use that for a demand gen campaign instead - 1 campaign targeting all locations. Adding keywords:

Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:

Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

    I added new buyer recommendation below what I wrote:

I want to flag something regarding the Google Ads account. We’re getting a policy warning related to business name mismatch, and after checking everything, it looks like the issue is coming from how the business identity is shown on the website.
 
Right now, the website header only shows the logo and doesn’t have the business name written in text. In the footer, it lists multiple names together: “Auto Brokers of Montana | AA and A Auto Rental | Fox Rent A Car.” There’s no clarification on how those names are related.
 
From Google’s side, this can look unclear because:
  •  The domain is usedcarsbillings.com
  •  The business name in Google Ads is Auto Brokers of Montana
  •  Multiple business names are shown on the site without structure
 
When their system crawls the page, it can’t clearly determine which business is the primary advertiser. That’s what usually triggers a mismatch or misrepresentation flag.
 
To fix this properly, I recommend we ask the client to:
  1.  Add “Auto Brokers of Montana” in clear text in the website header (not just inside the logo).
  2.  Update the footer so it clearly identifies the main legal entity, for example:
© 2026 Auto Brokers of Montana, LLC
DBA AA & A Auto Rental
(Only include Fox Rent A Car if it’s officially authorized and documented.)

subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

Displaying two numbers for the same ad dilutes the call-to-action and confuses the user. The Algorithm Picks a Winner. Since both are applied at the Account level and are therefore eligible for every ad impression in the account, the Google AI algorithm will use a real-time, impression-by-impression decision process to choose only one number to display.  The algorithm selects the single Call Asset it predicts will result in the highest Ad Rank, which is heavily influenced by the expected Call Conversion Rate (CVR) for that specific user, search query, device, and time of day.    This is why      your ad preview only shows one number—the preview tool defaults to the      most likely winner or a system default.  The numbers      will alternate, but the rotation is not random or even. The number you see      most often is simply the one that is currently performing (or predicted to      perform) better based on historical data. Performance Insight — Roosters Harley-Davidson SEM Campaign

Overall Trend

From Apr 22 – May 19 compared to Mar 25 – Apr 21:

	•	Total clicks across enabled campaigns decreased by 32 clicks
	•	Primary campaign decline:
    POW7756901_POW_Powell Broadcasting_Roosters Harley-Davidson_Primary_SEM
	•	Clicks dropped from:
	•	589 → 561
	•	Change: -28 clicks (-4.75%)

This is a relatively moderate decline, not a severe performance drop. The campaign is still maintaining traffic volume, but competitive pressure increased.



Main Insight

Competitors Increased Top-of-Page Presence

Google identified that your ads ranked above competitors less frequently during this period.

Competitors increasing visibility:

	•	ChopperExchange
	•	Dennis Kirk
	•	Sun & Fun Motorsports

Largest competitor movement:

	•	Sun & Fun Motorsports:
    +13% Absolute Top of Page Rate

This indicates:

	•	competitors became more aggressive in bidding,
	•	improved ad relevance,
	•	or increased budgets.

Your campaign likely lost:

	•	premium placements,
	•	higher CTR opportunities,
	•	and some high-intent traffic.


What This Likely Means

The issue is probably NOT:

	•	broken tracking,
	•	low demand,
	•	or campaign failure.

The issue is more likely:

	1	auction competitiveness,
	2	lower ad rank,
	3	weaker ad engagement,
	4	or insufficient bid aggressiveness.



Recommended Optimizations

1. Improve Ad Rank

Ad Rank is driven by:

	•	bid strategy,
	•	ad relevance,
	•	expected CTR,
	•	landing page experience.

Action

Refresh RSAs with stronger Harley-focused messaging.

Recommended Headlines

	•	New Harley-Davidson Bikes
	•	Used Harley Motorcycles
	•	Roosters Harley-Davidson
	•	Harley Deals Available Now
	•	Schedule A Test Ride Today
	•	Shop Harley Inventory
	•	Touring & Cruiser Motorcycles
	•	Billings Harley-Davidson
	•	Finance Your Harley Today
	•	Certified Harley Inventory


Recommended Description Angles

	•	Browse new and pre-owned Harley-Davidson motorcycles in Billings.
	•	Explore touring, cruiser, and performance Harley models today.
	•	Financing options available on select Harley-Davidson inventory.
	•	Visit Roosters Harley-Davidson and schedule your test ride today.



2. Tighten Keyword Intent

You may be competing too broadly.

Prioritize:

	•	Harley-Davidson branded intent
	•	local dealership searches
	•	inventory-focused searches
	•	buyer-intent searches

High-Intent Keywords

harley davidson billings
roosters harley davidson
used harley davidson
harley dealership near me
new harley davidson motorcycles
harley touring bikes
harley test ride
harley financing
motorcycle dealer billings
harley inventory


3. Reduce Broad Match Expansion

If using broad match aggressively:

	•	Google may be entering weaker auctions,
	•	causing lower CTR and weaker positioning.

Recommendation

Shift more spend toward:

	•	phrase match
	•	exact match
	•	top-performing search terms

    Overall account performance slightly declined week over week, with total conversions decreasing by 7.47%, resulting in 44 total conversions compared to the previous period. However, cost also decreased by 4.71%, which helped maintain an efficient CPA at $10.93. Based on Google’s attribution model, additional delayed conversions are still expected over the next 18 days, so final conversion numbers may continue to improve.
    
    The strongest performer during the period was the Sales/Montana campaign with 22 conversions, followed by the Sales campaign with 8 conversions and the Service campaign with 5 conversions. The Service campaign showed the largest positive movement with a 150% increase in conversions, indicating stronger demand and improved engagement from users actively searching for trailer service-related terms. The Sales campaign also increased by 31%, showing continued stability in core sales traffic.
    
    The largest decrease came from the Dump Trailer TF Geo campaign, which dropped by 60%. Auction insights indicate competitors increased visibility in overlapping searches, which likely impacted impression share and positioning. The Sales/Montana campaign also saw a moderate 12% decrease, but it still remained the top contributor for total conversions in the account.
    
    Search term insights continue to show strong intent around branded and localized trailer searches, especially terms related to “horse trailers for sale in Montana,” “Kalispell trailers,” and “trailer sales Billings MT.” Industry search demand is also trending upward nationally, particularly for horse trailers and enclosed trailers, creating additional opportunities to expand keyword coverage and capture higher-intent traffic.
    
    Audience insights show the highest-performing users continue to come from Commercial Vehicles in-market audiences, Truck & SUV Enthusiasts, and Motor Vehicle shoppers. These audiences generated strong engagement and conversion efficiency, confirming that the account is reaching users with high purchase intent. Asset insights also show messaging focused on inventory size, fair pricing, and Montana locations continues to resonate well with vehicle-focused audiences.
    
    Moving forward, the priority will be recovering lost volume from the Dump Trailer campaign while continuing to scale the stronger-performing Service and Sales campaigns. Additional keyword expansion, search term refinement, and audience-focused optimizations will help capture growing search demand and improve overall conversion consistency.

 I took a deep dive into the campaign performance from January 1 to April 15, 2026 and wanted to share what I’m seeing and what I’ve already been working on.

From a performance standpoint, the campaign is generating conversions (38 total at around $94 CPA), but there are a couple of key factors limiting call volume right now.

The biggest constraint is visibility. We’re currently only capturing about 14% impression share, while losing roughly 25% due to budget and ~61% due to rank. That means we’re missing a large portion of potential traffic, especially compared to competitors who are consistently showing higher on the page. Our top-of-page rate is only ~16%, which directly impacts inbound calls.

On the keyword side, performance is heavily concentrated in a few high-intent terms like:
	•	epoxy floor
	•	garage floor coating contractors near me
	•	garage floor epoxy
	•	branded searches

At the same time, a good portion of spend has been going toward broader or lower-intent keywords that haven’t converted.

Because of that, I’ve already made several optimizations:
	•	Paused underperforming keywords that were driving spend without conversions
	•	Removed redundant and overlapping keywords to reduce internal competition
	•	Tightened the keyword structure to focus more on high-intent epoxy and contractor searches
	•	Began consolidating similar keywords across ad groups to improve performance and signal strength
        • 	Reviewed the search query report and excluded irrelevant queries to improve traffic quality

From the competitive side, auction insights show that competitors like garageflooringpros and sharkfloorcoatings are outranking us and appearing more frequently at the top of the page, which also explains why volume hasn’t scaled with the budget increase.

So even though the budget increased, it’s currently being limited by rank, competition, and previous keyword inefficiencies, which is why calls haven’t picked up significantly yet.

The calls look good, some go abandoned and some go unanswered but most are good calls! I think forwarding them to his cellphone makes the most sense if no one is in office to take calls. Especially since they offer 24/7 emergency services.

Some Notes:
Phone calls perform best on Search, where intent is explicit. Pmax drives on display/youtube/lower intent interactions and harder-to-qualify leads
So switching to Sem could be a great move if calls are his primary focus but we would be starting over with the learning curve for Google so we could see a drop in calls or slow start since it is January. So keep that in mind. Also 3500 would be a great budget for SEM!

I think budget is great at 3500 ill never say no to trying to get more from the client as it can only help but I dont think its a driving factor here as conversions are really good and the campaign is doing good. Cost/conv can be lower its a bit on the hight side and I do want to get ctr up its a bit low. I can make optimizations to help with this.

We could add a Search campaign and pause the pmax one..for two reasons. One if the client ever wants to switch back, or two, if he wants to run both at the same time.

I have excluded fayettville from the geo. Our current raidus is 50 miles which is great but expanding to 60 could get us some new searches.

-Good call on your suggestion to route the calls to his cell, or a better number where someone will answer. Many of his calls are going unanswered/abandoned.  Those calls are going to be hard to know for sure if they were a legit lead or not, but the client needs a better system in place to ensure they are taking advantage of the leads they are paying for. The more calls that get answered will also help us understand more clearly which channels are working best.

-I see you are getting conversions from You Tube. I listed to a handful and agree they do not sound like the best leads. Either a wrong number, or no one is on the phone, or the call is getting abandoned. I only listen to about 6 or 7, you may want to do a further analysis and listen to more calls, specifically from that channel. Sometimes only looking at the data doesn't give us the full picture on how well a campaign is performing. If you're finding these are spam or low quality leads, then we can try a couple of different things. 
-First, add a integration trigger where you are only count a website call as a conversion that is 45-60 seconds long.  We can then provide Google better data, ie. a longer call could mean a more qualified lead. 
-We can also try adding a search campaign and use a fluid budget. You can still allocate a portion of the budget to pmax, so we can continue to use the full funnel, while also controlling more spend in search. In the past 30 days, we've spent about 57% of the budget on search. 

-If the client prefers to text, he would first need to answer the call, and then text back using his number. We've turned text messaging off our call tracking number. Text messaging in call rail does not work like a regular number. It won't send the message directly to their phone, but rather the client would have to log into call rail and view their messages through their platform. Its not ideal, and we wouldn't want users thinking they made contact via text, and then never receive a response so its better to turn it off unless the client will be checking their account throughout the day. 

Here are some suggestions to help improve your campaign -
-For Pmax, its important to add strong audience signals.  You added search themes that is good. You can also try and add some first party data, as well as some relevant in market data, ie. home and garden services, plumbing services, home improvement, home inspection, etc.

-With larger pmax budgets, dont feel like you always have to build just 1 asset group. You can build out multiple asset groups for different services, similar to how we structure our ad groups with search campaigns. You can then  set up specific audience signals, ad copy, images, videos, etc for each asset group.

-Try and add different video ratios - have you tried using asset studio yet? You may be able to resize an existing video, I would try that first. If its not really sizing correctly, then we can reach back out to the DCM.

-Try adding two more sitelinks to max those out

-Look at your search terms, are these all relevant? I see a lot of them look spot on, but noticed some that we may need to add as a negative. For example -construction companies in north Carolina, general contractor holly springs nc, excavator companies near me are some that stand out, are these relevant? Don't forget to check your search terms on pmax campaigns too!

Per our teams conversation

Hello! I am putting in a buyer rec to add a search campaign to our existing pmax and put it on a fluid budget. This tactic gives us more control and visibility over high-intent search traffic while still benefiting from pmaxs automation. Search campaigns allow us to capture users who are actively looking for specific keywords, improve  on what searches are driving results, and help guide budget. Sharing the budget lets Google dynamically allocate spend to whichever campaign is performing best at any given time, improving overall efficiency without increasing risk.

If we add a search campaign please keep in mind google may take a short adjustment period as it redistributes budget and traffic between the two campaigns. During this time, you might see small performance fluctuations, but this is normal and usually stabilizes quickly.

In terms of our search impression share. So with a $4,700 budget, a 30% Search Impression Share for pmax is still reasonable. At this spend level, pmax has to prioritize where it shows across multiple channels, so it won’t capture every available impression. If the campaign is hitting its CPA or ROAS targets, a 30% impression share simply means the system is being selective and efficient with budget.

For the text message issue. I think the easiest work around would be for the client to text customers  from the number he wants to use or tell them what number to text him on. However there may be another option. I have not had time to look into it yet but my TL just forwarded me an article we can take a look at. Here is an article that explains the text messaging feature in callrail - https://support.callrail.com/hc/en-us/articles/30896711642253-Sending-text-messages-in-CallRail In order for this to be enabled, the client must register for this feature.  Once they register, the messages are sent into the callrail inbox where the client can review and respond.  I believe there is also a feature where we can forward these messages to the client's cell. I dont know of any client that has actually done this though. The issue I could possibly see with this is if we track this as a conversion then the call and text from the same client may count twice. Also multiple texts may count also. Again I have not fully looked into it but after skimming it I have some questions I would need answered first to suggest this above the client simply just giving the person the correct number to text.

Mike Miller

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (Aug 24)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

Conversions dropped pretty sharply (from 7.06 down to 3.17, about -55%), even though spend only decreased slightly (~10%). Because of that, CPA climbed up to $67.79, so we’re paying significantly more per conversion right now.

From what I’m seeing, this doesn’t look like a budget or serving issue—the campaign is still spending and running normally. The bigger driver seems to be a drop in search demand and some shifts in the auction.

On the search terms side, a few of the higher-volume categories either brought in no conversions or declined week over week. For example:
	•	“interior designers bozeman” completely dropped off in conversions
	•	Other terms are still getting volume but not translating into actual leads

So it’s less about traffic quality breaking, and more about lower intent or weaker demand during this period.

Auction insights also show competition picking up. Advertisers like Home Depot are appearing more aggressively and increasing their position above rate, which means we’re likely getting pushed into less competitive positions or paying more for similar visibility.

Overall, this looks like a mix of:
	•	Lower search intent / demand week over week
	•	Stronger competition in the auction
	•	Traffic still coming in, but not converting at the same rate

Nothing fundamentally broken in the campaign, but definitely a short-term efficiency dip. I’d monitor closely over the next few days and start tightening up search terms (negatives, match types) if this trend continues.

This resulted in a CPA of $232. Since conversions can continue to attribute up to 2 days after an impression, performance may still adjust slightly as additional conversion data comes in.
    
    One important factor to consider is that the campaign is still in the learning phase after transitioning from Maximize Clicks to Maximize Conversions bidding. It is normal to see fluctuations in traffic volume, spend distribution, and conversion performance while the system recalibrates and gathers enough signals to optimize toward conversion outcomes instead of click volume. However, branded location searches such as “monteriors bozeman” saw lower conversion activity compared to the previous period.     continues resonating with homeowners and home improvement audiences, with the 1200×1200 creative remaining one of the stronger-performing visual assets.

As the campaigns continue learning under Maximize Conversions, performance is expected to stabilize and optimization should become more conversion-focused over time.

Lone Star – Budget Change Impact Review
 
Budget Timeline:
• July 17, 2025 – Budget increased to $4,500/month
• August 1, 2025 – Budget reduced to $2,500/month
 
Performance Summary:
In the week before the budget cut (July 24 to 30), the campaign generated an estimated 246 clicks, 4,470 impressions, 14 conversions, and spent around $980. After the budget was reduced (July 31 to August 6), results dropped to 142 clicks, 1,730 impressions, 8 conversions, and $467 in spend.
 
This means clicks dropped by 42 percent, impressions by 61 percent, and conversions by 43 percent. Despite the lower spend, the cost per acquisition improved slightly, going from around $70 to $58.
 
Key Takeaways:
    1.    Leads dropped – The 43 percent decline in conversions immediately after the cut shows fewer opportunities for sales.
    2.    Visibility shrank – A 61 percent drop in impressions means significantly less audience reach.
    3.    Traffic declined – Clicks fell by 42 percent, which directly impacted the flow of potential leads.
 
Recommendation:
The $4,500 budget in late July produced stronger performance across the board at a consistent and sustainable CPA. Cutting the budget disrupted momentum and reduced both visibility and lead flow. To recover results and drive continued growth, I recommend restoring the previous budget level so the campaign can scale effectively

subtasks.title: 15 Day Opts
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

Campaign Performance Insight (May 15–21, 2026 vs May 8–14, 2026)

Looking at the last 7 days, the campaign showed stronger engagement while maintaining stable spend.

Clicks increased by 14.55%, reaching 126 total clicks, while total cost slightly decreased by 0.74% to $529. At the same time, average CPC improved by 13% to $4.20, which means we generated more traffic without increasing spend and gained efficiency in how we acquired clicks.

From an auction perspective, our impression share is currently at 18% (-4%), which is tied with Hedrick Fire Protection at 18%. While overall visibility decreased slightly, competitor movement suggests increased competition in top placements rather than a demand decline.

One thing that stands out is top-of-page presence. Our Absolute Top of Page Rate is 20% (-2%), while competitors like Frontline Wildfire are appearing in the highest position more aggressively at 72% (+15%). This may indicate they are bidding more aggressively or prioritizing impression dominance.

The good sign is that the competitor landscape remained stable. no new advertisers entered the auction, so performance shifts are coming from existing competitors adjusting strategy instead of market saturation.

From Search Term Insights, we’re seeing stronger intent around residential fire protection services. Searches like:

	•	wc fire protection (+167%)
	•	residential fire sprinkler system (+250%)
	•	residential fire sprinkler system cost (+200%)
	•	fire sprinkler system repair

This suggests users are actively researching installation, pricing, and repair-related services, which could create opportunities to expand keyword coverage and tailor ad messaging toward residential intent.

Audience insights also show interesting behavior:

	•	Do-It-Yourselfers generated the strongest engagement (34.8% of clicks | 3.3x concentration)
	•	Avid Investors (30% | 2.5x)
	•	Home Automation Enthusiasts (29.1% | 2.2x)

This may indicate users are looking for property improvements, protection upgrades, and long-term home value investments—not only emergency service demand.

Next OPs:

	•	Review impression share loss and evaluate if top-performing keywords need bid adjustments.
	•	Expand keyword coverage around residential fire sprinkler installation, repair, and cost-related searches.
	•	Tes A/B focused on home safety, system upgrades, and residential protection.
	•	Consider testing Search Partners carefully since Google estimates additional reach potential, but monitor lead quality

First, 16 negative keywords were removed, and that opened up more opportunities for the ads to show. Some of the negatives were blocking relevant searches, so once those were lifted, the campaign started appearing in more auctions and reaching more users.

We also started outranking several competitors more often during this date range. Sites like mikehostilolawfirm.com and castanlecca.com saw a drop in outranking share compared to us. With our ads showing in higher positions more frequently, we naturally got more clicks and more engagement. 

Another big driver was the performance one from the ad group. That ad group alone jumped from 1 conversion to 8, and the projected conversions also increased significantly. subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.

subtasks.title: Last Opts Date (need for new cards)
subtasks.notes:
Notate KPI Metrics:
Either CTR or Leads, how is the KPI performing
Account pacing/budget:
Is it pacing appropriately per day/week/month
Any notes to DCM or ongoing issues:
Account suspensions, ad disapprovals and/or anything preventing the account from spending and performing
Check Conversion actions, form fills, DNR etc.:
Are they working, are they generating conversions, if not investigate
Address any notifications/recommendations:
In MC there is a notifications tab, address any issues there and clear the ones that are not applicable. For both outside MC and inside MC accounts, check the recommendations tab in google, are they applicable to your strategies yes or no? Dismiss if you have addressed.
Create New campaigns / ad groups.:
If you create new campaigns / ad groups note those to the DCM and in your optimization notes
RSA strength:
Minimum of good for all, aim for excellent. Sometimes brand and conquesting arnt able to get to good, if this is the case notify team lead
Image extensions:
After 3 months image extensions are available to you, requirement to add when you can. Pull images from the website or reach out to the DCM for more images, you can also contact your social counterpart for images since its a requirement on their side
Audiences / RT audience:
These should be set up from the beginning but we can expand as we do more opts, see what kind of search terms are being generated and see if there are opportunities you can leverage for audiences.
Adding keywords:
When reviewing your search terms see if there are any patterns and expand on them if there is an opportunity.
Negative Keywords (SQR):
This is vital for success and lead quality if you are using any type of broad match keywords and should be reviewed monthly.
Removing Non serving keywords:
If keywords do not serve any impressions over a 1 month period (excluding seasonal keywords) remove them from the account and adjust ad copy for the ads associated accordingly.
Changing ad copy (within limitations) to better reflect the serving headlines:
Match headlines / descriptions with keywords
Check Targeting / Geo:
Make sure your geo-targets match the ones in tapclicks.
Check change history:
Be sure to set your date range between the day you are optimizing an account and the day that you last did opts to see if any other email address has made changes to an account. Notify team lead right away.
